- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in subsequent days; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for 5–10 day horizon.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when price deviates >10% from 18-day moving average; adjust forecast toward historical mean if deviation >1.5σ.
- When sentiment is neutral or bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model often fails to capture downward momentum; apply lagged correction: subtract 1–3% per day for 3–5 day horizon.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to overestimate recovery; reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment is mixed or bearish.
